prior_review_check.area: Atomic state publication: Rust aliasing, compiler and x86 ordering
findings: Read actual f4_terminal and all Acquire observers. STATE remains one live AtomicU8, with UnsafeCell interior storage accessed through AtomicU8::as_ptr; there is no forged mutable/shared non-atomic Rust reference. Fresh symbols plus PIC arithmetic resolve the emitted pointer to the actual one-byte STATE symbol.

The store asm has default read/write memory effects and is neither pure, nomem nor readonly. Thus publication cannot be compiler-hoisted ahead of prior retained-owner memory writes, nor can later UART memory operations move before it. nostack and preserves_flags are truthful for this MOV; inputs are consumed but not modified.

Actual MOVB immediate3 at 0x26e9d6 is a nontearing one-byte x86 store to normal kernel memory. Release suitability depends on BOTH the compiler memory barrier and x86 normal-memory store ordering, not atomicity alone. No locked RMW or hardware fence is needed for this target store-release operation. AtomicU8::as_ptr emits only stack moves and RET, no ordering dispatcher or panic edges.

This is a target-specific inline-asm synchronization implementation, not a portable Rust Ordering::Release library call or a claim that arbitrary raw byte writes synchronize. The admitted runtime is single-vCPU/CPL0/IF0; Rust owner observers cannot concurrently reenter, and IRQ/NMI/fatal owner reentry is forbidden by the accepted policy. Unchanged Acquire observers and irreversible state>=SEALED policy remain intact. No SMP, device-memory, racing non-atomic access or generalized mixed-width guarantee is inferred.
